hints: Notice the observed $850 \text{ Hz}$ is greater than the emitted $800 \text{ Hz}$ - recall whether approach or recession compresses the sound waves.
For a source moving towards a stationary observer use $f_o = f_s v/(v - v_s)$ with $v = 330 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Rearrange to $v - v_s = v \times f_s/f_o$, calculate $330 \times 800/850$, then subtract from $330$ to find the drone speed in $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough: Observed frequency $850 \text{ Hz}$ is higher than source frequency $800 \text{ Hz}$. For sound, a higher pitch means the waves are compressed, so the drone must be moving towards the observer.
Use the Doppler equation for an approaching source and stationary observer: $f_o = f_s \times v/(v - v_s)$, where $v = 330 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ is wave speed and $v_s$ is source speed.
Substitute values: $850 = 800 \times 330/(330 - v_s)$. Rearrange to $330 - v_s = 330 \times 800/850$.
Calculate the effective wavelength term: $330 \times 800/850 \approx 310.6 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ in speed units.
Hence $v_s = 330 - 310.6 \approx 19.4 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, about $19 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ with sensible precision.
Magnitude about $19 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ directed towards the observer matches the table row. This is option C.

options.A: The speed $19 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ is correct but moving away stretches the waves and would give an observed frequency below $800 \text{ Hz}$, not $850 \text{ Hz}$.
options.B: Moving away from the observer cannot raise the observed $850 \text{ Hz}$ above the emitted $800 \text{ Hz}$, and $21 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ does not satisfy the Doppler equation.
options.C: Approaching shortens the observed wavelength so $850 \text{ Hz} > 800 \text{ Hz}$, and $f_o = f_s v/(v-v_s)$ gives $v_s$ about $19 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ towards the observer.
options.D: Towards the observer is the correct direction for an increased frequency, but $21 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ is too large and does not satisfy $850 = 800 \times 330/(330-v_s)$.
